logarithmic-functions-asymptote.alt: Graph of g(x) = 2 log base 2 of (x - 1), with a dashed vertical asymptote at x = 1 and points (2, 0), (3, 2), (5, 4) and (9, 6).

logarithmic-functions-shape.alt: Graph of y = log base 2 of x. It exists only to the right of the y-axis, drops without bound near the vertical asymptote x = 0, crosses the x-axis at (1, 0) and rises more and more slowly through (2, 1), (4, 2) and (8, 3), bending downward the whole way.

logarithmic-functions-moved.alt: Graphs of y = log base 2 of x, in blue with its dashed asymptote x = 0, and h(x) = log base 2 of (x + 4) minus 1, in green with its dashed asymptote x = -4. The graph of h is the blue graph moved 4 units left and 1 unit down; it crosses the x-axis at (-2, 0).
